newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM says neighbours helping combat rebellion.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM says neighbours helping combat rebellion.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Wednesday that the country was fighting terrorism on a war footing and that many neighbouring countries were helping it combat insurgency.

"We have been fighting terrorism on a war footing, we are meeting it effectively," Gujral told the Lok Sabha, the lower house of parliament. "We can take care of ourselves because the country has enough resilience power to combat such activities."
He was replying to an opposition lawmaker's question on government action against insurgency.
Gujral said India's relations with Bangladesh had improved over the past year and Dhaka was helping India fight terrorism in the region.
"With the new (Bangladeshi) goverment, our relations have undergone a qualitative change. Their government is cooperating and assisting us in this matter," Gujral said.
India and Bangladesh signed a landmark 30-year water-sharing treaty last December, removing a decades-old dispute over river water that had been the biggest obstacle to bilateral cooperation.
Gujral also applauded Bhutan's help. "Bhutan never encourages giving shelter to terrorists and whenever we need help it is provided," he said.

Dozens of guerrilla groups have been fighting for decades for independent homelands in India's northeast, which borders Bangladesh, Bhutan, Burma and China. The region is home to nearly 200 ethnic groups.
Gujral said the Himalayan kingdom of Nepal was also aiding India in stamping out insurgency.

The divided Himalayan region of Kashmir has been rocked by a bloody separatist revolt since 1990. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed in Kashmir over the past seven years.
Mostly Hindu India controls two thirds of the Moslem-majority territory and Pakistan the rest.

India says neighbouring Pakistan arms and trains the Kashmiri guerrillas, many of whom are fighting for merger with the Islamic state. Islamabad says it provides only moral and diplomatic support to the rebels.
